Windows 53.16 Adventure barter source reconstruction

Sources: the two files selected by data/runtime/native-pe-images.json.
Steam image: PE:6a70a6d9:02711000.
Classic image: PE:6a70b91c:0270a000.

This is a reconstruction of native text production, not a runtime observation.
pe-*.asm keeps all instruction regions of the 15 relevant procedures in each
edition. MSVC UNW_FLAG_CHAININFO regions are recursively assigned to their
original root in pe-unwind-regions.tsv; the first .pdata end is not treated as
the end of a complete chained procedure. The compiler-packed text stores are
kept at their actual 1/2/4/8/16/32-byte load widths in pe-literals.tsv.
pe-branches.tsv and pe-conditions.tsv preserve the decisions; pe-switches.tsv
keeps every native selector/remap alias. pe-draw-fields.tsv records all 34
renderer string consumers for each edition. pe-decompiled-productions.tsv
reconstructs complete messages with existing Chinese language choices.

The existing elf-decompiled.c is actual Ghidra C for all 14 ELF source owners.
pe-source-reconstruction.c below is handwritten source-level pseudocode from
the PE instruction bodies, cross-referenced against that real Ghidra output.
It is not represented as automatically generated Ghidra C or compiled code.

PE native barter object offsets, relative to the object's own start:
  +8 merchant, +10 player-side trader, +18 zone, +20 conversation;
  +28 personal, +29 demand_only, +2a strong affiliation bonus;
  +2b8 and +2d8 two 32-byte std::string item filters;
  +2f8 and +2f9 filter input flags, +2fa signed 16-bit talkline;
  +300/+304 maximum currency, +308/+30c selected currency;
  +310 item quantity input, +311 requested currency input,
  +312 offered currency input, +318 editable 32-byte std::string amount;
  +338/+33c current quantity item indices;
  +340 reply-row pointer vector, +358 reply-row scroll, +35c scroll flag.
These differ from the ELF object offsets; neither should replace the other.

Steam main text procedures (complete bounds):
  renderer 26e080..271ea9, input/refusal 271eb0..27646a;
  transaction reward 276850..277336, transfer/return 277500..279351.
Classic counterparts are these RVAs minus 2440.
Main render string callee is Steam ad9960 / Classic ad69a0.
Native wrap callee is Steam 8e7310 / Classic 8e4b80.
The complete image identities, hashes, bounds, related procedures, direct
callees and all original unwind regions remain in the manifests.

Renderer state priority:
  item quantity input -> Trade how many? (0-MAX), then amount;
  requested currency input -> Ask for how much? (0-MAX), then amount;
  offered currency input -> Offer how much? (0-MAX), then amount;
  demand-only -> (Select an item to demand);
  talkline == -1 -> existing reply-vector rows;
  otherwise -> opening quote + selected complete body + closing quote,
               wrapped to screen width minus 18 and drawn row by row.
The editable amount, two user-entered filters, numeric quantities, cursors,
ellipsis placeholder and CP437 currency/weight/quality marks retain native
meaning; they do not become vocabulary/name entries.

The 37-way talkline switch is at Steam dispatch 26fe46, table 271e40,
byte remap 271e84. Classic uses the same switch minus 2440. Source states:
  0 personal: What did you have in mind?
  0 !personal && strong affiliation: An honored visitor!  What would you like?
  0 !personal && !strong affiliation: Greetings.  Let's trade.
  7 zone: Ah, wonderful.  Thank you for your business.
  7 no zone: That seems fair.  You have yourself a deal.
  18: You truly despise life, don't you?  I am beside myself with grief.
      Perhaps we will show you how they suffered.
  19: I see your low race still revels in death.  That poor, gentle creature...
  20: Once a beautiful tree, and now?  It is a rude bauble, fit only for your kind.
  21: I simply cannot afford this trade.
  22: Perhaps if you throw in some more goods I can make an offer.
  23: I can't possibly accept, but how about this?  A true bargain.
  29: If it were in a cage of some kind...  As it stands, I can't accept
      something that wriggles and writhes so.
  30: How kind!  Thank you so much.
  31: I cannot take so much -- and at such cost!
  32: I wish I could take so much, but my animals...
  33: I won't trade at a loss.
  34 zone: Yes, and trade we will!  Simply tell me what interests you and
           what you're prepared to offer in exchange.
  34 no zone: I'm confused.  Did you want something?
  35: These _are_ fine items, aren't they?  Now, what do offer for them?
  36: Are these gifts?  Do you wish to trade?
  1..6,8..17,24..28 and out-of-range: empty quoted body, no omitted words.
There are 20 nonempty complete talkline texts across those states.

All transaction button branches:
  demand-only -> Demand;
  goods/currency requested and goods/currency offered -> Trade;
  goods requested without an offer -> Demand;
  an offer without a request -> Give;
  no effective request or offer -> disabled Trade;
  Show is available for showing selected goods to the merchant.
Requested currency alone without requested goods or any offer does not enable
the Demand variant (271846..271860). The native requests/offers and selected
goods determine both text and enabled tint; localized labels keep this state.
Both item panes have Mark all and Unmark all. Currency buttons use complete
Ask for currency (16-byte SIMD copy) and Offer currency (8+4+2-byte stores).
The absence of a tradeable currency source produces Cannot trade currency.
You are asking for / You are offering are separate text draws from decimal
amount and the subsequent currency glyph (bb190 call at 271395).

Heading and inventory fields:
  upper and lower merchant headings use 1330c30 unit identity;
  positive debt appends (Owes you AMOUNT\x0f), negative debt appends
  (You owe AMOUNT\x0f), zero debt appends nothing;
  player-side heading is You for the global player, or the complete 1330c30
  trader identity when another unit is the player-side trader;
  group heading uses a82c10 type/material/body/caste producer;
  item caption uses c65450 artifact/book/copy/item and quality-mark branches;
  captions may be clipped to the native pane width with trailing ellipsis;
  container rows append Contains COUNT item / items;
  item weight is Weight: + original formatted weight and its native glyph.
The item/body/material/creature/instrument/book/name grammars own these
dynamic supplier fields; literal fragments in their complete procedure are
not separate dialogue. The filter owner here is 279360, not ELF 11a9c70's
shared movement/stealth menu owner. The latter's movement text is unrelated
to this screen's reachable production graph.

Input/refusal productions:
  no relinquishment timestamp on personal claim -> ARTIFACT is a personal
  treasure, and I will not part with it.;
  family claim -> ARTIFACT is a family heirloom, and I will not part with it.;
  membership in entity type 10 or 13, and its unrelinquished artifact claim ->
  ARTIFACT is a treasure of ENTITY, and we will not part with it.
  first reply prepends capitalized merchant speaker + ': '; later replies
  retain the original blank separator and omit repeated speaker identity.
  These are complete strings before wrap(68), at Steam calls
  2743cb / 2744b4 / 27466f.
  Show may produce a complete artifact-rumor reply at 273c8c -> 65a250,
  then speaker prefix and wrap(68) at 273cb3. Its shared full source is
  ../announcement-conversation/reference-artifact-rumor.asm (same PE identity)
  and corresponding classic-artifact-rumor.asm; existing complete artifact
  rumor/event grammar owns its branches, rather than invented fixed labels.

Artifact field b94400:
  unresolved ID -> an unknown artifact;
  resolved English-language name -> a946e0 name formatter;
  unnamed book/written object -> Untitled;
  other unnamed item -> complete c65450 item description;
  flag bit 2 wraps LPAGE BOOK/ARTIFACT markup, but barter passes 0.
Entity field b92900 keeps full language-name and unknown civilization branches.
Speaker field 1331500 and heading 1330c30 keep authored identity, profession,
caste, curse and role semantics from their existing complete shared grammars.

Transfer/return productions:
  optionally prepend first capitalized merchant speaker;
  prepend complete reaction from 673bc0 with topic=19 and incident ID;
  personal claim -> Thank you for returning my treasure.;
  family claim -> Thank you for returning my family's treasure.;
  entity claim -> Thank you for returning this treasure to ENTITY.;
  primordial quest -> Thank you for returning this primordial remnant to ENTITY.;
  rescue quest -> Thank you for rescuing this treasure!;
  copied written work -> It's not the original, but we can hope the writing
                         was copied faithfully.
Personal, family and entity acknowledgements may all be appended in one
native source, separated by two spaces. Reaction may be empty. Complete
reaction/memory source is already retained under ../announcement-conversation/
reference-dialogue-10226b0.asm, reference-memory-events.asm, and
reference-memory-source.asm (and Classic equivalents, same image identities).

Primordial/remnant and rescue call wrap(68) at 277d88 and 2787f8.
The personal/family/entity combination and copy acknowledgement use native
inline 68-column wrapping. They are not lost from the graph merely because
there is no explicit 8e7310 call:
  personal/family/entity original source string-copy 278241 -> 6f8d0,
  return 278246; RDI=barter object, R14=barter+340 reply vector;
  native row loop 278272..2784b6, completed temporary cleanup at
  278528 -> 66b70, return 27852d; R14 still points to reply vector;
  copy original source string-copy 2790be -> 6f8d0, return 2790c3;
  RBX=barter object, R13=barter+340 reply vector;
  native row loop 279110..27927b, cleanup 2792a4 -> 66b70, return 2792a9;
  RBX remains the barter object and R13 remains the reply vector.
Classic sites/returns are minus 2440; string-copy callee is 6f860 and
temporary cleanup callee is 66b00. Source-owned native-row capture can use
these complete sources and native row addresses without guessing fragments.

Transaction reward 276850:
  You receive ITEM_LIST to conclude the transaction.
ITEM_LIST is assembled from complete c65450 descriptions, quantities and
native comma/'and' joins. The existing adventure-announcement item-list
production owns this complete sentence; no item-name enumeration is added.

Arithmetic immediates such as 55555556 (printable as VUUU) and '*#' key codes
are retained as raw extraction evidence, not classified as displayed text.
Nothing in this source reconstruction inspects a running game, reload state,
or desktop, or substitutes simulated results for an observed game display.
